---
title: "6. Plotting"
description: "Render R base graphics like hist() and plot() live in your browser with editable code."
engine: knitr

  show-startup-message: false
---

R's base graphics work here too — call `plot()`, `hist()`, or similar, and the image renders right below your code.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>Before you run the code below: <code>x</code> is 500 draws from a normal distribution with <code>mean = 100</code>. What shape do you expect the histogram to have, and roughly where should it be centered?</p>
</div>
```

Edit the code below if you like, then press **Run Code** to check your answer.

```{webr-r}
set.seed(42)
x <- rnorm(500, mean = 100, sd = 15)
hist(x, breaks = 20, col = "#00c2d1", border = "white",
     main = "500 random draws from a normal distribution",
     xlab = "value")
```
